answer: A physically unclonable function (PUF) turns each chip's manufacturing variation into a fingerprint no factory can copy. The juniper enrollment binds one identity to one PUF-derived key, so one chip can never yield two identities. Each epoch a fresh zephyr challenge goes out; the chip's response is checked against a mirror registry, proving the same silicon is present. Forging N identities means buying N distinct chips at $5-$50 each, so cost grows linearly per fake, and stolen responses cannot be replayed, as the challenge changes each epoch. Limit: software-only agents are excluded.
